VS Code opens with the test workspace kanban-ac10-ws. The .kanban/ folder is visible in the explorer and contains test-worktree-missing.md with workspace: '/nonexistent/worktree/path/that/does/not/exist'. The extension is loaded from the installed VSIX. No dialogs, no pickers blocking interaction.

2 · Open Kanban Board via command palette

Command palette opened via Cmd+Shift+P. 'Kanban Board: Open' is typed and confirmed. The Kanban Board tab opens in the editor area.

3 · Board loaded with the test card

The Kanban board renders fully. The 'In Progress' column shows the test card 'Test: Missing Worktree Warning'. The sidebar overview lists 1 total feature. React mounted and rendered successfully via the inlined bundle script (workaround for a VS Code resource-URL pipeline corruption that doubles large bundle contents).

4 · Click card; trigger Build with AI

Clicking the 'Test: Missing Worktree Warning' card opens the FeatureEditor on the right side, showing the card frontmatter (Status, Priority, Assignee, etc.) and body. We post startWithAI directly to the extension via the stashed vscode API, simulating a user clicking Build with AI → Claude → default. The extension's startWithAI handler runs and calls AgentLauncher.launch() with the test feature.

5 · Warning notification appears; fallback succeeds

AC 10 verified: AgentLauncher detects that the worktree path '/nonexistent/worktree/path/that/does/not/exist' does not exist, shows the warning notification 'Worktree path not found — launching in workspace root' (bottom-right), and falls back to the workspace root (kanban-ac10-ws). The terminal launches Claude in the workspace root as confirmed by the 'Accessing workspace: /private/tmp/kanban-ac10-ws' message in the terminal.
